a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines (names, without asserting or proving) the following proposition: For all types P, D, E, and R, for every structure t consisting of four functions c1 : P -> Set D (assigning a subset of D to each element of P), c2 : D -> Set E (assigning a subset of E to each element of D), c3 : D -> R, and c4 : R -> E, and for every element r of R: let A (t.D19 r) be the set of all q in P for which there exists an element o in c1 q with c3 o = r, and for each q in P let U(q) (t.D20 q) be the set of all e in E for which there exists an element o in c1 q with e in c2 o (the union of c2 o over all o in c1 q). If there exist a function S from A to A and an element p in A such that U(p) and U(S p) have empty intersection, then there exists an element o in D such that (1) o belongs to c1 q for at least one q in P, (2) c3 o = r, and (3) c4 (c3 o) is not in c2 o. Note what is and is not required: no finiteness, nonemptiness, or compatibility assumptions are placed on P, D, E, R, or c1, c2, c3, c4; in the hypothesis (t.D21 r), no properties are required of S beyond being a function from A to A, disjointness of U(p) and U(S p) is required only for the single chosen element p (not for all elements of A), and S p is not required to differ from p (so the hypothesis is logically equivalent to the existence of elements p, p' in A, not necessarily distinct, with U(p) disjoint from U(p')); and in the conclusion, the witness q in P showing o in c1 q is not required to be p or S p."}
translation: Target defines (names, without asserting or proving) the following proposition: For all types P, D, E, and R, for every structure t consisting of four functions c1 : P -> Set D (assigning a subset of D to each element of P), c2 : D -> Set E (assigning a subset of E to each element of D), c3 : D -> R, and c4 : R -> E, and for every element r of R: let A (t.D19 r) be the set of all q in P for which there exists an element o in c1 q with c3 o = r, and for each q in P let U(q) (t.D20 q) be the set of all e in E for which there exists an element o in c1 q with e in c2 o (the union of c2 o over all o in c1 q). If there exist a function S from A to A and an element p in A such that U(p) and U(S p) have empty intersection, then there exists an element o in D such that (1) o belongs to c1 q for at least one q in P, (2) c3 o = r, and (3) c4 (c3 o) is not in c2 o. Note what is and is not required: no finiteness, nonemptiness, or compatibility assumptions are placed on P, D, E, R, or c1, c2, c3, c4; in the hypothesis (t.D21 r), no properties are required of S beyond being a function from A to A, disjointness of U(p) and U(S p) is required only for the single chosen element p (not for all elements of A), and S p is not required to differ from p (so the hypothesis is logically equivalent to the existence of elements p, p' in A, not necessarily distinct, with U(p) disjoint from U(p')); and in the conclusion, the witness q in P showing o in c1 q is not required to be p or S p.

divergences.description: In the conclusion, Target requires o ∈ t.D17 (there exists some physical configuration p with o ∈ obs(p)), whereas Lemma 3.3 and Definition 3.4 in the source passage only ask for o ∈ O (the ambient class of datasets). This is a harmless strengthening that is already guaranteed by the proof and matches the author's claim.

Through the ambient structure S3 and the falsification predicate D18, Target idealizes inference content as a total single-valued map c3 : D → R, inference as a total single-valued function c4 : R → E depending solely on inference content, and falsification specifically as c4 (c3 o) ∉ c2 o. The quoted passages do not commit to single-valued (rather than set-valued or partial) inference.
Lemma 3.3 and Lemma 3.5 are merged into a single statement corresponding directly to Lemma 3.5, with Lemma 3.3 recoverable as an immediate weakening by dropping the conjunct t.c3 o = r.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the combined content of Lemma 3.3 and Lemma 3.5—that an o_r-substitution yields a falsification at a dataset with inference content o_r—with only minor modeling idealizations in S3/D18 and a harmless strengthening to realizable datasets.
